title: Meanings of materials through sensorial properties and manufacturing processes
research_question: To investigate the importance of sensorial properties and manufacturing processes in attributing particular meanings to materials, to explore the effects of certain manufacturing processes on meanings, and to identify which properties and processes play a more important role than others for creating particular meanings.

participants.description: 7 PhD Researchers and 18 students from the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering of Delft University of Technology, Delft, The Netherlands.
participants.recruitment: Participants were informed one week in advance and asked to select products.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Participants selected 5 products each (total 125 products) expressing five given meanings (aggressive, nostalgic, professional, sexy, toy-like) where materials predominantly played a role. They could bring visual representations if physical products were not possible.

Visual representations of 13 sensorial properties (e.g., roughness, glossiness, transparency) and 8 manufacturing process categories (e.g., shaping, joining, surface treatment). Each property was shown with three visuals (two opposite ends, one moderate level). Each process was shown with at least three visuals of sub-processes or end-results.

measures.construct: Importance of sensorial properties and manufacturing processes for meaning attribution
measures.instrument: Five-point Likert scale questionnaire with visual representations of properties and processes

findings.mechanism: Hardness is a commonly used sign for attributing meaning to materials.
Roughness is a commonly used sign for attributing meaning to materials.
Glossiness is a commonly used sign for attributing meaning to materials.
Colorfulness is a commonly used sign for attributing meaning to materials.
Color intensity is a commonly used sign for attributing meaning to materials.
Strength is a commonly used sign for attributing meaning to materials.
Weight is a commonly used sign for attributing meaning to materials.
Odorous property was not considered important for meaning attribution.
Production volume was not considered important for meaning attribution.
Decorative joining was not considered important for meaning attribution.
Shaping through molding was not considered important for meaning attribution.
Invisible joining was not considered important for meaning attribution.
Functional joining was not considered important for meaning attribution.
Transparency was not considered important for meaning attribution.

findings.antecedent: Material properties (e.g., hardness, roughness, glossiness, colorfulness, color intensity, strength, weight)
findings.consequent: Overall mean importance for meaning attribution
findings.mechanism: Sensorial properties generally received higher mean scores than manufacturing processes in overall evaluation.
findings.quote: sensorial properties generally received higher mean scores than manufacturing processes (Fig. 4).

findings.antecedent: Material properties: Hardness, dark colors (black), glossiness, material combinations (metal and dark colored plastics), rough, cold
findings.mechanism: These properties are commonly associated with the 'aggressive' meaning through verbal appraisals.
findings.quote: Hardness received the highest mean score in attributing aggressiveness to products

findings.antecedent: Material properties: Patterns, heavy, warm, dark colors (brown)
findings.mechanism: These properties are commonly associated with the 'nostalgic' meaning through verbal appraisals.
findings.quote: For nostalgic, participants were mostly looking for materials that were such as popular 50 years ago.

findings.antecedent: Material properties: Smooth, hard, cold, dark colors (black), matte, semi-transparent, mass-produced, brushed, coated; Manufacturing processes: invisible joining, functional joining, shaping for details
findings.mechanism: These properties and processes are commonly associated with the 'professional' meaning through verbal appraisals and quantitative ratings.
findings.quote: invisible joining, functional joining and shaping for details.

findings.antecedent: Material properties: Smooth, hard/soft, cold/warm, light colors (white), intense colors (crimson), glossy/matte, semi-transparent
findings.mechanism: These properties are commonly associated with the 'sexy' meaning through verbal appraisals.
findings.quote: while transparency and smoothness were very much used for conveying the meaning of sexy

findings.mechanism: Roughness was highly rated for conveying the 'sexy' meaning.
findings.quote: roughness got the highest ratings for the meaning sexy.

findings.antecedent: Material properties: Smooth, light, strong (unbreakable), ductile, primary colors (red, blue, green, yellow), color combinations, elastic
findings.mechanism: These properties are commonly associated with the 'toy-like' meaning through verbal appraisals and quantitative ratings.
findings.quote: color intensity and colorfulness were two leading properties in toy-like products

findings.antecedent: Material properties: Texture and wall thickness
findings.mechanism: These properties were frequently mentioned by participants as noteworthy factors in meaning attribution during verbal appraisals.
findings.quote: Texture and wall thickness, sensorial properties that are pretty much related to manufacturing processes, were often mentioned to be noteworthy factors in meaning attribution.

mechanisms: Materials' sensorial properties and manufacturing processes act as 'signs' that users interpret to construct meanings and values for products.
Meaning attribution is based on the overall impression of the material and the product it is embodied in, with sensorial properties influencing this impression.
Manufacturing processes contribute to sensorial experiences and meanings by creating particular surface treatments or combinations of materials.
moderators: Product context (e.g., geometrical shape, color, overall product impression)
Context of use (e.g., hurting effect of rough surface, burning handle)
implementation_implications: Designers need insights into the role of materials for creating particular meanings attributable to products.
Designers should look beyond obvious properties to understand the roots of a material's meaning.
Further studies should focus on meaning creation in materials, particularly through colors.

tables.description: Manufacturing process categories (and sub-processes) used in the main study
Summary of the verbal appraisals with a set of product samples, listing associated materials and properties for each of five meanings (Aggressive, Nostalgic, Professional, Sexy, Toy-like).
Results of one sample t-test comparing mean scores of each property/process against a test value of 2.99 (likely the neutral midpoint of the 5-point scale).

limitations: Participants had difficulties selecting products expressing a particular meaning predominantly through their materials, with other product properties (e.g., geometrical shape, color) often playing a crucial role.
The effects of a material on a product's meaning were found to depend much on the product in which the material is embodied.
Aggressive meaning was difficult to express through material properties; shape was more influential.
Context of use (e.g., hurting effect of rough surface, burning handle) appeared as an effective factor in meaning attribution.
Personal experiences and backgrounds affected decisions, especially for nostalgic meanings.
Transparency and elasticity received lower ratings than expected, suggesting they might be less important or context-dependent.
Manufacturing processes generally received lower mean scores than sensorial properties, and were often not easy for participants to recognize in products despite clear visual representations.
Judgment of a particular manufacturing process requires a more focused assessment of a product.
It was challenging for participants to understand all sub-processes and evaluate their implications.
Some sub-processes (e.g., sewing, injection molding) could be presented individually for better clarity.
